headline: GOLD HITS LOWEST SINCE AUGUST 2025 — Spot Falls to $3,578 as US PCE Surge Reignites Federal Reserve Rate Hike Fear
snippet: Spot gold plunged to its lowest since August 2025 on November 26, trading as low as $3,578 per ounce after hotter-than-expected US PCE inflation data revived expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike; silver fell below $41 before stabilising near $42. The print marks a continuation of November's brutal rout for precious metals, with gold now down more than 10% from its October highs and testing the conviction of investors holding through the selloff on the structural bull thesis.

headline: MACRON ORDERS FRANCE TO STOCKPILE CRITICAL MINERALS — Strategic Reserves Program Launches 2027 to Break China Dependence
snippet: French President Emmanuel Macron announced on November 26 that France will establish strategic reserves of rare earths and other critical minerals starting in 2027, explicitly to reduce dependence on Chinese supply; the declaration was made as China's export control policies on gallium, germanium, and antimony remained in a state of uncertainty ahead of the November 27 deadline. France's decision to build state-level strategic mineral reserves is the most concrete Western government action in the current de-risking cycle and could accelerate similar reserve-building programs across Germany, Italy, and the UK.

headline: AUSTRAL RESOURCES CLOSES $80.7M HAMMER METALS DEAL — Kalman Copper Deposit Locks In Queensland Growth for ASX Mid-Tier
snippet: Austral Resources (ASX) completed its court-approved A$80.7 million scheme of arrangement takeover of Hammer Metals on November 25, 2026, adding the Kalman copper deposit to its Queensland copper portfolio in a deal that transforms it into one of the more copper-concentrated mid-tier miners on the ASX. Deals done cheaply in bear markets historically produce the strongest long-term returns, and Queensland's copper processing infrastructure is built for scale — making Kalman a strategically priced addition at the bottom of the copper price cycle.

headline: COPPER CRASHES BELOW $12,000/T FOR FIRST TIME SINCE MARCH — AI Demand Doubt Deepens Bear Market to 20% Below September Peak
snippet: LME copper fell below $12,000 per tonne on November 23 for the first time since March 2026, as markets priced in growing doubt about AI-driven data centre demand that had underwritten the commodity's record run to $14,694 per tonne in September — a 20% rout in under three months. The sell-off contrasts sharply with still-elevated Chinese physical import premiums near $450 per tonne on the Yangshan premium, suggesting the decline is a futures market repricing rather than a demand destruction event.

headline: NORDIC RESOURCES KOPSA DRILL HITS GOLD-COPPER IN PLANNED PIT WASTE ZONES — 1.52Moz AuEq Deposit Grows in Finland
snippet: Nordic Resources (ASX: NNL) reported that the first five holes from its second-half 2026 drill program at Kopsa, Finland, intersected shallow gold-copper mineralisation inside zones previously classified as waste within the planned open pit — a resource expansion outcome that improves the grade-distribution model at the 1.52 million ounce AuEq Kopsa deposit. Finding economic mineralisation in areas previously defined as waste is a low-capital-intensity way to increase the processed grade and reduce dilution impact, two levers that directly improve project-level economics without additional drill metres.

headline: VANTAGE METALS DRILLS COPPER AT KALAHARI — 2.74m at 1.06% Cu on First Hole at Chanoga Prospect in Botswana
snippet: Vantage Metals (ASX: VAN) reported its first drill results from the Chanoga prospect at the Kalahari copper project in Botswana on November 25, with the initial hole returning 2.74 metres at 1.06% copper — a first confirmation of mineralisation at a greenfields target in one of the world's most prospective copper belts. The Kalahari copper belt hosts several of the world's largest undeveloped copper deposits not held by majors; a first-hit confirmation on a new prospect in this corridor is precisely the catalyst that attracts institutional attention before multi-hole follow-up drilling is established.

headline: DUKETON MINING STARTS 2,500m GOLD DRILL PROGRAM IN WA — Astro, Astro West and Odie Targets at Barlee Project Activated
snippet: Duketon Mining (ASX: DKM) announced the start of a 2,500-metre drill program at the Astro, Astro West, and Odie targets within its Barlee Gold Project in Western Australia on November 26, testing geological models developed after its 2024 regional mapping campaign. Deploying drill capital into new targets during a gold price selloff is counter-cyclical positioning: when gold recovers, the results are already in hand and re-rated against a higher spot price rather than competed for by other explorers' simultaneous press releases.

headline: ONTARIO CUTS EXPLORATION PERMIT RED TAPE — Single Permit to Cover Multiple Land Parcels Under New Mining Reforms Package
snippet: Ontario's government announced a mining reform package on November 24, 2026, led by a single-permit system that would allow explorers to cover multiple separate land parcels under one exploration licence rather than applying individually for each — a material reduction in permitting time and cost for junior companies assembling multi-parcel claim blocks in Northern Ontario. For TSX-V explorers in Ontario's prolific mining camps, reduced permitting friction directly translates to lower administrative overhead and faster drill-to-results cycles, the two cost centres most damaging to junior mining economics at this stage of the commodity cycle.

headline: BRAZIL APPROVES EMA RARE EARTH EXPLORATION REPORTS — BCM Clears Regulatory Milestone in Bahia State Deposit
snippet: Brazilian Critical Minerals (ASX: BCM) disclosed that Brazil's national mining agency approved the final exploration reports for its Ema rare earth project in Bahia state on November 25-26, clearing a key regulatory hurdle before a development decision; permitting approvals, funding commitments, and offtake agreements are the next milestones. Brazil's Northeast is one of the least explored rare earth jurisdictions globally, and the ANM approval opens the door to a resource upgrade announcement as BCM moves toward a pre-feasibility study.

headline: DISCOVERY ALERT: GOLD MINERS FALL 2-3X HARDER THAN SPOT — Why Retail Investors Keep Getting Blindsided by Mining Equity Beta
snippet: A Discovery Alert analysis examines why gold mining stocks typically sell off two to three times harder than spot gold during commodity price corrections — driven by operating leverage, fixed-cost structures, and the reflexive deleveraging of retail positions — and argues that understanding this beta dynamic is essential to sizing mining equity positions correctly during a bull cycle. The November rout has demonstrated this leverage in real time: miners that were up 80-100% year-to-date have given back 40-50% of those gains on a spot gold correction that amounts to only 10-14% from peak.

headline: THE CASE FOR MINING EQUITY DIVERSIFICATION — Stage, Metal and Jurisdiction Are the Real Portfolio Levers, Not Market Timing
snippet: A Discovery Alert analysis argues that mining equity portfolio risk is best managed through diversification across company development stage, commodity, and jurisdiction rather than through attempting to time commodity price cycles — with the November selloff cited as a case study in why stage and jurisdiction diversification smoothed volatility more than metal selection alone. Retail investors who concentrated in gold equities through the 2026 bull run would have experienced materially smaller drawdowns had they also held exposure across copper, uranium, and silver developers in multiple jurisdictions.
